newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian peso dips in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Colombian peso dips in quiet trade.

text.p: Colombia's peso dipped 10 centavos to 1,062.6 against the dollar in quiet trading, interbank traders said.
Traders said the markets were waiting for the government to formally repeal a recently-introduced law to tax foreign debt, following a Constitutional Court ruling last month.
The government introduced a 6 percent tax on all newly contracted foreign debt under the terms of a state of economic emergency in mid-January.

But in a controversial ruling last month the Constitutional Court declared the emergency unconstitutional, meaning the government must revoke its package of emergency decrees. So far, however, the government has not taken that step.
Dealers reported 231 trades worth a total $90 million, about half the daily average. The peso opened at 1,061.8 and reached an intraday high of 1,061.2. The low was 1,062.7 pesos.
